source: ALTA 2026 Seller Impersonation Fraud Study via HousingWire and NAR

headline: Fake sellers are
*on the rise*
slides.fig_caption: Of title firms saw at least one seller impersonation attempt in 2025
slides.sub: More than double the 28% in ALTA's 2024 survey.

slides.title: Firms seeing *an attempt*
slides.note: One in four firms that saw an attempt also *paid a claim*. Half of those disclosing costs averaged more than $100,000.

slides.title: Who scammers *target*
points: Vacant land: *82%* of firms call it a common target, still No. 1.
Vacation homes, rentals and primary residences all rose sharply since 2024.

slides.title: Signs of a *fake seller*
points: The seller avoids meetings and *won't get on a call*.
They push for a mail-away signing or *pick their own notary*.
*87%* of firms see spoofed contact info.
*58%* say image or voice deepfakes are at least somewhat common.

slides.title: Verify sellers *before listing*
slides.body: Confirm identity early, reach owners through contact details you find on your own, and mail a letter to the property address. Take extra care with vacant land, absentee owners and remote-only deals.
